## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sālakajātaka* (Ja 249) is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection. The framing story opens with the verse incipit *Ekaputtako bhavissasīti* (“Like my own son”) and is set while the Buddha was dwelling at Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī [Fausböll 1879]. The narrative occasion concerns a prominent elder (*mahāthera*) who had ordained a young boy as a novice; because the elder mistreated and harassed him, the novice disrobed and left the monastery, prompting the elder to pursue him and attempt to coax him back with affectionate promises [Fausböll 1879].
